evidence_quotes.quote: Endogenous knowledge and practice regarding the environment in a Nahua community in Mexico
We expose some representations and practices related to the natural environment among Nahua peasants in a village located at the western boundary of Puebla and Guerrero states, in Mexico.
The use of some local, vegetal resources, and the local perception of changes, mainly in the water availability, is documented.

raw_response.plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both the narrow rule-type reading and the plain institutional/governance wording of Criterion 2 because the study examines indigenous cultural and sacred representations of the natural environment, vegetal resources, weather, and migration rather than any legal, administrative, regulatory, or institutional governance mechanism.
raw_response.rationale: This qualitative ethnoecological study examines endogenous Mesoamerican cultural and sacred representations of the natural environment, vegetal resources, weather conditions, and perceived environmental water availability among Nahua peasants in Mexico. Although it mentions perceptions of environmental water availability, it examines cultural/sacred belief systems and migration pressures rather than any legal, administrative, regulatory, tenure, tariff, or institutional governance mechanism governing domestic water or sanitation service access (E03).
